name: Antidepressants / anxiety meds

card.summary: Rx mental-health drugs used for anxiety and depression; not appearance treatments, with modest effects and real side effects.
card.note: FDA warning on suicidality in young people; discontinuation symptoms reported.

quick.overview:
Antidepressants are prescription drugs for depression and anxiety disorders. In looksmaxxing they appear as a medication option for appearance-related distress.

They are not appearance treatments, and no study tests them for that.
quick.mechanism: Most block reuptake of serotonin, sometimes with norepinephrine, raising signaling in the brain.
quick.risks: Reported effects include sexual dysfunction, weight change and emotional blunting. An FDA warning covers suicidal thinking in under-25s, and stopping suddenly can cause discontinuation symptoms. Prescription only.

lead: Antidepressants and anxiety medications are prescription drugs used for depression, anxiety disorders, OCD and PTSD. They are not cosmetic treatments, but they come up in looksmaxxing communities because mood and anxiety shape how a person looks and presents: energy for training and grooming, willingness to go out and be seen, posture, eye contact and ease in conversation. Forum members discuss them as a way to lower the social anxiety or low mood that can undercut an otherwise improved appearance.[1][12]

The main antidepressant classes are SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclics and MAOIs, and the anxiety-medication group also includes benzodiazepines, buspirone, hydroxyzine and the beta blocker propranolol, which is used off-label for performance anxiety.[1][19][20][21] Meta-analyses find antidepressants outperform placebo in depression by a modest margin; for anxiety disorders the drug-placebo effect size is about 0.3.[1] A 2023 umbrella review of antidepressant trials in people with depression alongside medical illness reported small to medium effect sizes.[2]

Looksmaxxing threads also raise appearance-related questions about the drugs themselves, such as whether they affect skin, collagen, testosterone or weight. A 2025 network meta-analysis ranked individual antidepressants on physiological changes including weight, blood pressure and lab values.[3] Common reported adverse effects include sexual dysfunction, weight change and emotional blunting.[1]

chain: More energy and willingness to train, groom and socialise
Calmer, more open presentation of one's looks
angle.text: People who take these medications for a diagnosed condition often describe being better able to keep up with exercise, skincare, sleep and social life, all of which feed into how they look and come across. Some looksmaxxing forum members also discuss anxiety medication specifically for social confidence.

infobox: SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs, MAOIs; also benzodiazepines, buspirone, hydroxyzine, beta blockers [1][20]
Prescription only (propranolol also Rx-only in the US, UK and Australia) [21]
Propranolol used off-label by performers and speakers [21]
Body dysmorphic disorder, treated with SSRIs and CBT [23]

paras: Antidepressants are prescribed for depression, anxiety disorders, OCD, PTSD, chronic pain and some eating disorders.[1][19] Some drugs hold specific approvals; paroxetine is approved for social anxiety and PTSD, and paroxetine and escitalopram are FDA-approved for generalized anxiety disorder.[1][20] Antidepressants are also studied for neuropathic pain, where an international pain-society review of randomised trials assessed several drug classes.[4]

For social anxiety disorder, Wikipedia describes CBT as the first-line treatment, with SSRIs the usual medication choice; approved options include paroxetine, sertraline, fluvoxamine, venlafaxine and phenelzine, and medication acts faster while CBT's benefits tend to last longer.[22] Propranolol is used off-label for performance anxiety, and pregabalin and mirtazapine have also been used.[22]

No trial has tested antidepressants as an appearance treatment. In looksmaxxing forums, users describe them as a route to lower anxiety and improved mood, while other threads collect opinions on anxiety and social-anxiety medications.[12][14] The chain members describe is indirect: calmer mood and less anxiety make it easier to keep up with training, skincare, sleep and social settings, which in turn show in how a person looks and comes across.

Appearance preoccupation itself is a recognised treatment target. In body dysmorphic disorder, an overwhelming focus on a perceived flaw, SSRIs and CBT are both described as effective, with SSRIs said to ease obsessive-compulsive and delusional traits.[23] The same article notes that many people with the condition seek cosmetic treatment that typically does not resolve their distress, and that surgeons and psychiatrists are advised to work together to screen patients.[23]

SSRIs block reuptake of serotonin through the serotonin transporter, and six are widely marketed: citalopram, escitalopram, fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, paroxetine and sertraline.[19] They are first-line for anxiety disorders, with full effect taking about four to six weeks and anxiety sometimes rising at first.[20] SNRIs such as venlafaxine, which reached the market in 1993, also act on norepinephrine.[20]

subs.h: Benzodiazepines, buspirone, hydroxyzine and beta blockers
paras: Benzodiazepines such as alprazolam, lorazepam and diazepam act quickly and are used for short-term anxiety management; the literature describes drowsiness, memory impairment and a risk of dependence, with withdrawal possible if stopped rapidly.[20] Buspirone is a 5-HT1A agonist used for generalized anxiety and does not carry the same dependence profile, but is slow to act and is not particularly effective for social anxiety.[20] Hydroxyzine, an antihistamine, was FDA-approved in 1956 as Atarax and is used for anxiety.[20]

Propranolol, a beta blocker developed by James W. Black in the 1960s and marketed as Inderal in 1965, eases physical symptoms such as tremor and a racing heart rather than anxious thoughts directly.[21] A 1987 survey by an orchestral musicians' conference found 27 percent of members used beta blockers for performances.[21] Black received the 1988 Nobel Prize for the work, and propranolol's evidence base for anxiety disorders is described as limited: a 2016 and a 2025 systematic review found no clear benefit over placebo or benzodiazepines for social phobia or panic disorder.[21]

The first antidepressants, the MAOIs and tricyclics, appeared in the 1950s; iproniazid was found by accident while the tuberculosis drug isoniazid was being developed, and imipramine was first studied as an antihistamine.[1][20] SSRIs arrived in the 1980s, led by fluoxetine (Prozac), discovered in 1974 and FDA-approved in 1987, and SNRIs followed in the 1990s.[1][20] Esketamine, an NMDA antagonist, was introduced in the 2010s.[1]

Effects over placebo are modest, around 30 to 50 percent of people do not respond to a given drug, and critics argue trial design and publication bias inflate benefit.[1] A 2018 meta-analysis of 21 antidepressants found all outperformed placebo, though the certainty of evidence was rated moderate to very low, and an analysis of FDA trials found modest average benefit.[19] There is no consistent evidence that depression is caused by low serotonin.[19]

A trial of 141 patients with depression or anxiety disorders compared antidepressants with running therapy under a partially randomised patient-preference design and examined both mental and physical health outcomes.[5] A 2024 network meta-analysis reported that exercise modalities such as walking, jogging, yoga and strength training reduced depression scores compared with active controls.[6] A 2021 trial examined maintaining versus discontinuing antidepressants in primary care.[7]

Common effects include dry mouth, weight changes, dizziness, headaches, akathisia, sexual dysfunction and emotional blunting.[1] Mirtazapine and paroxetine are associated with weight gain, and bupropion and venlafaxine with weight loss.[1] One study of 1,022 patients reported sexual dysfunction in 57 to 73 percent of those on SSRIs, against 24 percent on mirtazapine and 4 percent on moclobemide.[1] Emotional blunting, reduced intensity of both positive and negative emotions, is linked mainly to SSRIs and SNRIs.[1][19]

A 2025 network meta-analysis compared antidepressants against placebo on weight, cholesterol, glucose, heart rate, blood pressure and other measures, finding differences between individual drugs.[3] A systematic review also catalogued oral manifestations such as dry mouth in people on these drugs.[8]

An FDA warning describes increased suicidal thinking and behavior in children, adolescents and young adults, highest in the first one to two months; an analysis reported odds ratios of 1.62 for ages 25 and under, 0.79 for ages 25 to 64 and 0.37 for 65 and over.[1] Other documented risks include serotonin syndrome when serotonergic drugs are combined, bleeding risk, QT prolongation with citalopram and escitalopram, and a switch to mania in bipolar disorder.[19]

Roughly 20 to 50 percent who stop suddenly report discontinuation symptoms, which may include nausea, dizziness, sleep trouble and 'brain zaps'; tapering reduces the risk, and paroxetine is associated with more discontinuation symptoms than fluoxetine.[1][19] Post-SSRI sexual dysfunction, sexual symptoms persisting after stopping, is described as having uncertain prevalence and contested status; the European Medicines Agency recommended label changes for selected SSRIs and SNRIs in 2019, and fluoxetine has carried a warning on persistent sexual side effects since 2011.[19]

On looksmax.org, discussion ranges from people asking about prescriptions for anxiety to threads on keeping testosterone up while taking them.[13] Some posters describe starting or stopping specific drugs and the effects they noticed.[15][16] On T Nation, members mention antidepressants such as mirtazapine alongside testosterone therapy and treat low testosterone and depression as separate matters.[17] Hacker News threads debate whether antidepressants are over-prescribed while still helping some patients.[18]

Wikipedia reports that propranolol, on the WHO list of essential medicines, ranked 69th among US prescriptions in 2023, with more than 9 million prescriptions.[21] Its off-label use by performers has extended to precision sports such as archery and shooting, and a shooter at the 2008 Olympics lost medals after testing positive for it.[21]

No studies found for looks-related anxiety or appearance outcomes. Trials of the drug class address general conditions: an antidepressant safety study in young people with anxiety, depressive and obsessive-compulsive disorders (n=569),[9] and a registered trial comparing sertraline with virtual-reality exposure for social anxiety disorder.[10] A 2023 meta-analysis of maintenance-phase treatment compared relapse rates between antidepressants.[11]

timeline.event: The first MAOIs and tricyclic antidepressants appear [1].
James W. Black develops propranolol; it is approved in 1964 and marketed as Inderal in 1965 [21].
Fluoxetine (Prozac) is FDA-approved, the first SSRI; a survey of orchestral musicians finds 27 percent use beta blockers [20][21].
Venlafaxine, the first SNRI, enters the market [20].
FDA analyses lead to a boxed warning on suicidality in young people [1][19].
Fluoxetine labelling adds a warning on persistent sexual side effects [19].
A 21-antidepressant meta-analysis finds all outperform placebo with moderate to very low certainty [19].
The EMA recommends label changes on persistent sexual dysfunction for selected SSRIs and SNRIs [19].

lore.intro: Looksmax.org members discuss antidepressants and anxiety medication as tools for mood and social confidence, and with questions about side effects on skin, hormones and weight.[12][13]

claims.claim: Antidepressants might damage collagen or age the skin
claims.believers: Forum posters have asked whether the drugs could harm collagen or age the skin, usually in the context of skin concerns.
claims.experts: No published studies examine antidepressants and skin collagen; reviews of side effects list metabolic, cardiovascular and oral effects.[3][8]

claims.claim: Antidepressants lower testosterone, so levels must be actively maintained
claims.believers: A thread asks how to maintain testosterone while on most antidepressants, reflecting a belief that the drugs suppress it.[13]
claims.experts: The trials listed here do not report on testosterone; their documented adverse effects include sexual dysfunction.[1]

claims.claim: Anxiety medication helps with social confidence
claims.believers: Threads on best social-anxiety medications and eager posts about starting a prescription show members seeing medication as a way to feel more at ease around others.[14][15]
claims.experts: Paroxetine holds an approval for social anxiety, and a registered trial is comparing sertraline with virtual-reality exposure for it.[1][10]

claims.claim: Antidepressants dull feelings rather than improve mood
claims.believers: Some forum posters say the drugs do not make people happier but only blunt distress, a view that echoes the emotional blunting listed among reported side effects.[1]
claims.experts: Meta-analyses report modest benefit over placebo in depression, with emotional blunting listed among reported adverse effects.[1][2]

claims.claim: Propranolol calms the body for social situations and performances.
claims.believers: Performers and speakers use it for tremor and a racing heart, and about 27 percent of surveyed orchestral musicians in 1987 reported beta-blocker use [21].
claims.experts: Wikipedia describes it as occasionally used for performance anxiety, easing physical symptoms, while a 2016 and a 2025 systematic review found no clear benefit over placebo for social phobia or panic disorder [21].

claims.claim: Antidepressants cause weight gain that changes how you look.
claims.believers: Members of appearance-focused communities raise weight and physique as a concern when considering a prescription, alongside skin and testosterone questions [13].
claims.experts: Weight gain is associated with mirtazapine and paroxetine and weight loss with bupropion and venlafaxine, and a 2025 network meta-analysis ranks drugs by weight change [1][3].

claims.claim: Sexual side effects can persist after stopping.
claims.believers: Some patients report lasting symptoms, called post-SSRI sexual dysfunction [19].
claims.experts: The EMA recommended label changes in 2019, Health Canada could neither confirm nor rule out a long-lasting link, and the condition's status as a distinct diagnosis is contested [19].

claims.claim: Treating appearance anxiety with drugs addresses the root of a 'flaw'.
claims.believers: Some posters see medication as a way to lower distress about how they look [12].
claims.experts: For body dysmorphic disorder, Wikipedia reports that SSRIs and CBT are both described as effective, and that cosmetic procedures typically do not resolve the distress [23].
